## Reproduced gate defect
At PR #29 head `9511fca43e748aeb097d4e5031137dd356e3e27f`, both Node 22 and 26 jobs fail in `npm run identity:check` with `added absolute home path`, before functional tests execute. Strict PM health passes.

- [PR #29](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/pull/29)
- [Node 22 job](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/actions/runs/40478199644/job/122101576234)
- [Node 26 job](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/actions/runs/40478199644/job/122101575822)
- [Exact gate source](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/blob/9511fca43e748aeb097d4e5031137dd356e3e27f/scripts/identity-gate.ts)

## Reproduction and cause
The commit adds four tracker/history files importing #27 and #28. The imported public #27 body contains ordinary prose:

`The exact mismatch/root cause has **not** been isolated`

The added-line scanner's POSIX root-home alternative `/root(?:/|\b)` also matches the root-home substring inside `mismatch/root cause`: it has a right boundary but no appropriate left path boundary. This phrase occurs in the imported item and its append-only history. Inspection of all four added patches found no actual absolute home path causing this failure.

A bounded local check extracted and evaluated the exact source regex (no Git operations or tracker mutation): eight assertions passed, confirming that `mismatch/root cause` and `+body: mismatch/root cause` match, as do true absolute paths (the root user's home directory, a file inside it, and files under placeholder Linux and macOS home directories); ordinary prose without the slash and `./relative/file` do not.

## Expected / actual / impact
Expected: preserve the private-path guard while allowing innocuous public issue prose through the gated sync workflow.
Actual: harmless issue text prevents both Node CI jobs from reaching functional tests, blocking delivery of the imported tracker records.

This is a pm-swarm consumer identity-gate false positive, not evidence of a private-path leak or a functional test assertion failure. Imported PM records are `pm-swarm-github-44bd244dd53c-27` and `pm-swarm-github-44bd244dd53c-28`; they own the separate lifecycle findings, not this gate defect. The canonical settings item `pm-swarm-y972` requires a private-path guard, so disabling it is not an appropriate fix.

## Acceptance / regression criteria
- Add negative controls for ordinary slash-separated prose such as `mismatch/root cause`, including its JSONL/TOON representation.
- Retain positive controls for actual absolute POSIX and Windows home paths, with realistic quoting and punctuation.
- Keep auditing the intended post-baseline commit history; do not weaken approved-identity checks or rewrite existing append-only tracker history to hide the failure.
- Verify the gated import can pass identity checking on both supported Node versions; report functional-suite outcomes separately.

## Limits and duplicate check
Evidence comprises the two hosted job logs, immutable source/patch inspection, and the isolated exact-regex check. No full functional suite was rerun. All-status repository issues/PRs and all 26 canonical tracker records at this head were checked; no existing owner of this particular false positive was found. PR head rechecked unchanged immediately before filing.

> Fixed by #48, merged as eeb9cd0. The identity gate no longer matches home paths with a regex. It resolves path tokens component by component: path tokens are found at a Unicode-aware path start and resolved in one linear pass, with POSIX tokens split on slashes only and Windows tokens on both separators. So prose such as "mismatch/root cause", relative names and web routes are allowed, while absolute home paths are refused, including dot-segment, Windows, file-URL and extended-length forms. The exact sentence from this issue is in the allow corpus. identity-gate.ts has 100% coverage, and identity:check over the branch history reports no violations. #29, the sync PR this blocked, now passes its gate after a branch update.
